per_window.text: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and the similar in size to Earth. It has a diameter of 12,104 kilometers and orbits at an average distance of 108.2 million kilometers. Venus rotates very slowly, and its rotation is retrograde, meaning it turns in the opposite direction to most planets. A single day on Venus lasts about 243 Earth days, which is longer than its year of 225 Earth days. Venus therefore has the longest day of any planet. The atmosphere of Venus is about 96 percent carbon dioxide, with thick clouds of sulfuric acid. Surface pressure is about 92 times the pressure on Earth. A runaway greenhouse effect makes Venus the hottest planet, with a surface temperature of about 465 degrees Celsius. Venus has no moons.

per_window.text: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only planet known to support life. It has a diameter of 12,742 kilometers and orbits at an average distance of 149.6 million kilometers, which is defined as one astronomical unit. Earth rotates once every 23.9 hours and completes one orbit in 365.25 days. It has one natural moon. About 71 percent of the surface is covered by oceans. The atmosphere of Earth is mostly nitrogen, at about 78 percent, with about 21 percent oxygen and small amounts of other gases. Average surface temperature is roughly 15 degrees Celsius. Liquid water is stable on the surface, which is essential for life we know it.

per_window.text: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and is often called the Red Planet because of iron oxide dust on its surface. It has a diameter of 6,779 kilometers and orbits at an average distance of 227.9 million kilometers. A day on Mars lasts about 24.6 hours, and a year lasts 687 Earth days. Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos. The atmosphere is thin and about 95 percent carbon dioxide. Average surface temperature is about minus 63 degrees Celsius. Mars has the largest volcano in the Solar System, Olympus Mons, which rises about 21.9 kilometers. It also has a huge canyon system called Valles Marineris. Evidence suggests that liquid water once flowed on the surface.

per_window.text: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and is famous for its bright ring system. It has a diameter of 116,460 kilometers and orbits at an average distance of 1.43 billion kilometers. Saturn rotates quickly. A day on Saturn lasts about 10.7 hours, and a year lasts about 29.4 Earth years. Saturn is the least dense planet, with an average density of 0.687 grams per cubic centimeter, which is less than the density of water. The rings of Saturn are made mostly of water ice, along with some rock and dust. Saturn has 146 known moons. Its largest moon, Titan, has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane and ethane.

limitations: The paraphrase support check is deterministic and narrow; it is not a general semantic equivalence model.
The Experiment 21 development set is small and manually labeled.
The final policy can miss genuine contradictions, such as dev21_c1, but remains conservative for unsupported cases.
The fixed benchmark has only 33 cases, so results should not be treated as population estimates.

final_report.objective: Determine whether paraphrase recognition can be improved without sacrificing the improvements from Experiment 20.
final_report.diagnosed_failure_mechanism: The remaining Experiment 20 benchmark failures (p1 and p2) were not relevance-filter failures. The NLI model assigned neutral to the cited premise/claim pairs, so the confidence and relevance policies abstained and returned insufficient_evidence.

development_set_design.purpose: Independent paraphrase, lexical-overlap, contradiction, insufficient, and irrelevant-citation checks.

new_policy.name: paraphrase_aware
new_policy.rule: Start from the Experiment 20 relevance-aware NLI policy; when the final result is insufficient_evidence with a neutral label and a cited window passes the conservative deterministic paraphrase check, promote it to supported.
